prompt.context: Our client is Akron Tires, an international tire manufacturer. Despite being a large player in the competitive tire industry, Akron Tires' performance has declined the last three years and they have hired us to reverse this trend.
prompt.question: Akron Tires specifically wants to increase its margins of its North American business segment within the next three years. How would you approach this problem?

clarifying_info.q: What is Akron Tires' business model?
clarifying_info.a: Akron Tires sells tires to OEMs such as Ford and GM, as well as to large retailers such as Sears and Walmart.
Akron Tires is the 2nd largest tire producer in the industry with 23% of the market. The 1st and 3rd largest players have market shares of 28% and 19% respectively.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's weighted average cost of capital (WACC)?

exhibits.title: Akron Tires 2016 Revenue Mix and Segment Sales/Costs
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing 2016 North American tire revenue mix by segment, and a table showing units sold and variable costs (in $000s) for 2016 and 2015 by segment. Total 2016 Akron Tires North America tire revenue was $4.50B.

exhibits.title: Tire Industry Segment Data — Projected CAGR vs. Average Industry Contribution Margins
exhibits.shows: A bubble chart plotting tire segments by projected 5-year CAGR (x-axis) and average industry contribution margin (y-axis). Bubble size represents market size. Segments shown include Passenger Car Tires, Commercial Truck Tires, Construction Truck Tires, Motorcycle Tires, Aircraft Tires, and Racecar Tires. A note states that Passenger Truck/SUV tires (9% projected CAGR, $18B market size, 23% industry contribution margin) are not shown on the chart.

data.note: Passenger Truck/SUV: 9% projected CAGR, $18B market size, 23% industry contribution margin. Other segments visible on chart with varying CAGRs (ranging approx. -3% to 5%) and contribution margins (approx. 10% to 30%). Passenger Car Tires are in the lower-left (low CAGR, low margin). $10B reference bubble shown.

framework: Revenue levers: existing customers/distribution channels, new customers, product mix optimization, new products, pricing/elasticity, promotional strategy
Cost levers: corporate overhead, direct/indirect plant costs, supply chain
External factors: changes in customer preferences (autonomous vehicles, low gas prices driving more miles), industry dynamics

questions.prompt: What do you observe from Exhibits 1a and 1b together? What hypothesis would you form before calculating?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate synthesizes both exhibits before diving into math. Exhibit 1a shows Passenger Car tires account for 40% of revenue but the highest unit volume (22.5M units), implying lower per-unit prices. Exhibit 1b shows Passenger Car tires have the lowest margins and projected negative/flat growth. Passenger Truck/SUV tires show the highest projected CAGR (9%) and a large market ($18B). Hypothesis: Akron's largest revenue segment (Passenger Car) is declining; the client should investigate growing Passenger Truck/SUV tires.

questions.prompt: Calculate Akron Tires' 2016 contribution margins for each of its main segments. How do they compare to industry averages?
questions.guidance: Use Exhibit 1a revenue mix percentages and total revenue of $4.5B to derive segment revenues, then subtract variable costs. Compare to industry averages from Exhibit 1b. Key insight: Passenger Truck/SUV and Construction Truck margins are below industry averages, signaling room for improvement.

math.setup: Total 2016 North America Revenue = $4.5B. Segment Revenue = $4.5B x revenue mix %. Contribution Margin = (Segment Revenue - Variable Costs) / Segment Revenue.
steps: Commercial Truck: Revenue = $4.5B x 15% = $675M; Costs = $519.75M; CM = ($675M - $519.75M) / $675M = 23.0%
Passenger Truck/SUV: Revenue = $4.5B x 25% = $1,125M; Costs = $900M; CM = ($1,125M - $900M) / $1,125M = 20.0%
Construction Truck: Revenue = $4.5B x 10% = $450M; Costs = $337.5M; CM = ($450M - $337.5M) / $450M = 25.0%
math.answer: Commercial Truck: 23%, Passenger Car: 15%, Passenger Truck/SUV: 20%, Construction Truck: 25%. Passenger Truck/SUV (20%) is below the industry average of 23% per Exhibit 1b; Construction Truck (25%) is also below its industry average shown on Exhibit 1b.

questions.prompt: The client only has one manufacturing plant in North America that produces truck tires, running at capacity. Additional truck tires are shipped from European plants at lower margins. The client is considering building a new plant in Mexico. What should the client consider when making this decision?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure brainstorming into clear MECE categories. Financial — Revenue side: additional volume, pricing strategy, growth expectations beyond 5 years, timeline to recognize revenue, path to market share capture. Financial — Costs: plant construction cost, operating costs (labor, utilities), raw material sourcing and tariffs on natural rubber, working capital and opportunity cost. Qualitative: US union backlash, FX currency risk, NAFTA/trade policy uncertainty, Mexican business laws/regulations, alternative options (lease, joint venture vs. build).

questions.prompt: The client expects to finish plant construction in 1 year at a cost of $400M (paid at end of Year 1). Once running, the plant generates $400M revenue and $300M costs in Year 2, growing at 5% per year thereafter. What is the NPV of building the plant? (WACC = 25%)
questions.guidance: This is a growing perpetuity NPV problem. A good candidate identifies the growing perpetuity formula and correctly discounts construction cost back one year. An excellent candidate completes the full calculation including the extra step of discounting the perpetuity value back from Year 1 to Year 0.

math.setup: WACC = 25%, growth rate g = 5%. Construction cost = $400M paid at end of Year 1. Annual cash flow starting Year 2 = $400M revenue - $300M costs = $100M, growing at 5%/year.
steps: Value of growing perpetuity at Year 1 (start of cash flows at Year 2): $100M / (0.25 - 0.05) = $100M / 0.20 = $500M
Discount perpetuity value back to Year 0: $500M / 1.25 = $400M
math.answer: NPV = +$80M. The project is positive NPV based on the client's projections.

brainstorming.prompt: What should the client consider when deciding whether to build a new manufacturing plant in Mexico?

categories.name: Financial — Revenue
ideas: How many additional tires do they expect to sell?
Would they maintain prices despite having lower costs?
What is the growth expectation beyond 5 years?
How soon can they build the plant and start recognizing revenue?
How do they expect to capture additional market share?

categories.name: Financial — Costs
ideas: How much will it cost to build the plant?
What are the operating costs — labor, utilities?
How will they receive raw materials and what are tariffs on importing natural rubber?
Do they have sufficient working capital, and what is the opportunity cost of deploying $400M?

categories.name: Qualitative / Strategic
ideas: Potential backlash from US union factory workers
Foreign exchange (FX) currency risk (MXN vs. USD)
Recent NAFTA uncertainty and trade policy risk
Are there alternatives to building — leasing, joint venture?

recommendation: Akron Tires should prioritize growing its Passenger Truck/SUV tire product line, which has the highest projected CAGR (9%), a large market ($18B), and current margins (20%) below the 23% industry average — indicating room for improvement
Building a new manufacturing plant in Mexico is a viable opportunity to expand truck tire capacity and improve margins, with a positive NPV of approximately $80M based on client projections
risks: Trade policy and NAFTA uncertainty could impact costs and cross-border logistics
FX risk with Mexican peso could erode projected margin improvements
US union relations may be strained by offshoring production to Mexico
Actual construction costs and ramp-up time may exceed projections, reducing NPV
Market share capture assumptions may be optimistic given competitive market (Akron is 2nd at 23% share)
next_steps: Conduct detailed due diligence on plant construction costs and operating cost assumptions in Mexico
Analyze competitive response from the #1 player (28% share) to a capacity expansion
Evaluate alternative capacity options (leasing, JV with Mexican manufacturer)
Develop a detailed demand forecast for Passenger Truck/SUV tires in North America
Assess options to reduce costs and improve margins in the Passenger Car segment given its large revenue base
